docs.title: Welcome to neo-apoli's documentation!
docs.text:
This page contains the surface level information regarding the mod, how it works, and what it provides for users to make data packs with.

neo-apoli is a rewrite of the Apoli mod by Apace, which provides an API for providing "powers" to entities via data packs.

docs.title: General information
docs.text:
• neo-apoli provides a context-based system to allow certain types, such as actions and conditions, to interconnect with powers in a dynamic manner. This also allows for features like "value providers," which are types that can provide a dynamic value (e.g: an entity's health as a value for a field).
  • Apoli and neo-apoli aren't compatible with each other due to how different their codebases are, so make sure that you create a new world/server.

docs.title: Action Types
docs.text:
Action types define how an action should operate on a context. Depending on the action, it can also pass the inherited context to its types that also use a context.

!!! note Some if not most action types require certain context parameters to function. Make sure to check the page for the corresponding action type that you want to use.

docs.title: Condition Types
docs.text:
Condition types define how a condition should test a context. Depending on the condition, it can also pass the inherited context to its types that also use a context.

Note

Some if not most condition types require certain context parameters to function. Make sure to check the page for the corresponding condition type that you want to use.

docs.title: Power Types
docs.text:
A power type defines how an instance of a power should function. It also contains the additional required/optional fields used for parsing.

Note

Each power type, unless stated otherwise, supports an optional active_condition field which determines whether the power is considered active. If the field is absent, the power will be considered as always active.

Note

Every power type provides and requires the neo-apoli:this_entity context parameter, which refers to the entity holding the power.

Some power types may provide certain context parameters that can be used in actions/conditions/value providers, so make sure to check their corresponding pages for more information.

docs.title: Callback Block Break
docs.text:
Invokes an action upon the player breaking a block.

Type ID: neo-apoli:callback/block/break

Context info

This power type provides the following context parameters:

Parameter Description neo-apoli:broken_block The block broken by the player. neo-apoli:broken_side The side at which the player broke the block.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Field Type Default Description on_break_action Action The action to invoke when a block is broken. only_when_harvested Boolean Provider false Determines whether the action should only be invoked when the block is broken with its correct tool. priority Integer 0 Determines the order (1) of which powers of this type will be iterated. About priorities

The instances of this type will be sorted in its natural order meaning that instances that have a lower priority value will be executed first before those that have higher priority values.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
    "type": "neo-apoli:callback/block/break",
    "on_break_action": {
        "type": "neo-apoli:set_entity_on_fire",
        "ticks": 20,
        "entity": "this"
    },
    "active_condition": {
        "type": "neo-apoli:is_block_of_type",
        "block_type": "minecraft:magma_block",
        "block": "broken_block"
    }
 }

This example sets the entity on fire if the block they broke was a Magma block.
